The internal hemorrhoids prolapse with straining and go back on their own. That defines second degree hemorrhoids, so the code is K64.1. Bleeding is part of this hemorrhoid category, so it needs no separate code. No external cause applies.

I am relying on this code being unchanged in the FY2027 (October 1, 2026) release. I don't know of a change to the K64 category, but I could not check it against that release.

["K64.1"]

The documented diagnosis is glaucoma suspect in both eyes, open angle with borderline findings, low risk. That maps to category H40.01 (open angle with borderline findings, low risk), and the 6th character 3 gives the bilateral code, **H40.013**.

No other codes are supported:
- There is no injury or external cause.
- No comorbidities are documented.
- The normal test results are not separately coded.

I don't know of any FY2027 change to this code, but I haven't checked it against the October 1, 2026 release itself.

```json
["H40.013"]
```

The answer is right ring finger trigger finger, M65.341.

- **Trigger finger:** The physician's assessment is trigger finger of the ring finger. This maps to the M65.34- subcategory, which needs laterality.
- **Laterality:** The physician's note does not say which hand. Official Guideline I.B.13 lets laterality come from other clinicians' documentation in the record. The clinic nurse's entry from the same visit records the right ring finger, so the code is M65.341.
- **No external cause codes:** The note states there was no injury.

```json
["M65.341"]
```
